```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)


knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)

def.chunk.hook  <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("chunk")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(chunk = function(x, options) {
  x <- def.chunk.hook(x, options)
  paste0("\n \\", "footnotesize","\n\n", x, "\n\n \\normalsize")
})

knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "") # removes ## in output

```

types of anomalies
- point anomaly
- contextual anomaly
- collective anomaly

methods for anomaly detection (from wikipedia)
- Parametric-based: Z-score, Tukey's range test, Grubbs's test
- Density-based techniques: k-nearest neighbor local outlier factors, isolation forests
- neural networks (IF and LOF recommended by Lucero when i emailed him)
- clustering
- many more

we should prolly focus on teaching the parametric and density methods
